title: Establish pilot runtime boundary and executable contracts
goal: Translate the verified pilot scope into runtime ownership dependency edges executable contracts and test fixtures before implementation.
inputs: canonical MVP dependency roadmap and pilot plan
outputs: uniquely owned product-runtime/context-envelope boundary with no executable product code
explicit preimplementation runtime security ownership with no fabricated coverage
pilot-local executable contract bound to PILOT-CONTEXT-001 and CAP-SET-004
positive and negative tenant/environment/permission fixtures defined before implementation
zero-external-runtime-dependency policy proven by dependency audit
invariants: no unresolved blocking decision is silently defaulted
pilot scope remains bounded and decomposed
security and correctness floors remain mandatory
security_properties: tenant scope and authority contracts remain mandatory where applicable
external product-runtime dependencies remain denied unless explicitly approved
pilot cannot weaken existing validation gates
acceptance_tests: runtime dependency audit reports one runtime boundary and zero dependencies
boundary-edge audit reports no undeclared local dependency edge
fixtures cover permission denied, tenant change, environment mismatch, expiry, missing tenant, wildcard tenant and unsafe return-origin

performance_budget.rationale: pilot must prove the engineering path without unbounded runtime or CI cost
metrics: pilot lot stays inside complexity budgets
existing E8 efficiency floors remain green

migration.rationale: scope and contract work precedes product persistence

rollback.strategy: revert the bounded E9 lot while retaining verified E0-E8 foundation

definition_of_done: pilot runtime root is uniquely owned
reserved runtime boundary has explicit security ownership before performance/runtime implementation
selected Product Spec contracts are executable test fixtures without changing Product Spec
negative tenant and permission cases are defined before implementation
